title: Service Brake Application
description: Observe graduated B1, B2 and B3 requests and compare speed and brake indications.

steps.instruction: Apply P2 to build speed before demonstrating service braking.
Confirm that the speedometer reads more than 2 km/h.
Select B1 and observe the initial service-brake request and brake indications.
Select B2. Compare the greater brake request with the current speed response.
Select B3. Explain how service braking differs from an emergency brake request.

learningObjective: Explain controlled service braking and the role of brake pipe and brake cylinder readings.
operatingConditions: Braking steps are illustrative and not representative of a particular vehicle’s stopping performance.
expectedObservations: The speedometer shows deceleration after service-braking requests.
Brake cylinder and brake pipe displays have different labels and meanings.
The displayed pressures are illustrative values and must not be used as real rolling-stock specifications.
debriefQuestions: What is the difference between a service-brake request and emergency braking?
Why must brake-pressure readings be interpreted alongside speed?
